The vision

What is MannaFish?

Take 2, keep one, give one.

The vision of MannaFish is to nurture people in their faith, and equip them to do the same for others.

It’s been said, “Give a man a fish, and you feed him for a day. Teach a man to fish, and you feed him for a lifetime.”

The multiplying of the two fish and five loaves began when one lad gave what he had to Jesus, and the result was a miracle (John 6:9–13).

This is the vision of MannaFish: take 2, keep one, give one. Give thanks, read the Scriptures, and pray.

Why is MannaFish free?

Because the vision behind MannaFish is to help people become gift givers.

A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.Proverbs 18:16

We believe a gift also makes room, and makes a way, for someone to hear about the greatest gift ever given.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son.John 3:16

A free gift is never free.

Someone always pays the price. Jesus paid with His life. A gift costs the giver something too.

But a gift is God’s way of demonstrating His love.

For God so loved the world, that He gave His one and only Son.John 3:16

So MannaFish is always a free gift. It is never sold and never resold. You cannot buy a MannaFish shirt, hat, decal or anything that carries the MannaFish name. It may only be given away. The cost is carried by the followers and sponsors who give.

Receive first. Then give.

You cannot give what you have not received. Jesus rose while it was still dark and went to a quiet place to be with the Father. He received freely from the Father, and gave freely to us.

Freely ye have received, freely give.Matthew 10:8

So start each day with the devotional. Feed yourself first, then be ready to give.

Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you.1 Peter 3:15

The 2 Fish Challenge

Wherever MannaFish is given away, at a coffee shop, a bookstore or a church lobby, take two: one for you, and one for a friend.

Every gift points to the free daily devotional, and carries an invitation from the one who gave it.

Will you pay the price?

Are you a Christian business owner, a bookstore, a church, an evangelist, a teacher, a pastor, a podcaster, a content creator, a Christian musician, a movie producer or an actor, and you want to share the gospel by giving gifts? This is a great place to do it.

Sow into other businesses and ministries and let them stock their ponds for giving. Or stock this pond, and we will pay it forward.

The goal is to keep MannaFish free. And everyone who gives a gift also gives an invitation: a QR code on the back to their church, ministry, podcast or gathering.

Why gather?

Every MannaFish is an invitation into connection, community, and growing together in faith.

He that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.Matthew 12:30
The heart of it

What is “2 Fish”?

You’ve heard the old proverb: give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime. At MannaFish we read it through the eyes of the One who fed the thousands.

In John 6, a boy brings five loaves and two small fishes — an ordinary lunch — and places it in Jesus’ hands. Blessed and broken, it feeds a multitude, with baskets left over. That’s the “2 Fish.”

Two fish means one for me, and one for you. First I take the Word and apply it to my own life. Then I give it away — and I teach the next person to do the same. A meal becomes a multiplication.

“There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?”John 6:9 · KJV

It’s the pattern of the manna in the wilderness: gather enough for yourself, and enough for those who cannot yet gather for themselves. Nobody goes without, and everybody learns to gather.

And here is the freedom in it — we are laborers together. One plants, another waters, but God gives the increase. That takes the pressure off, and puts the glory where it belongs.

What the name means
Manna — “What is it?”

Bread from heaven.

When bread appeared in the wilderness, Israel asked “man hu?” — “what is it?” That very question became its name: manna. It fell fresh each morning, enough for the day — God’s daily provision from heaven (Exodus 16).

Centuries later, Jesus said, “I am the bread of life … the living bread which came down from heaven.” The manna was a picture; He is the true Bread. And His Word is our manna — daily, from heaven, gathered fresh.

“I am that bread of life.” · John 6:48
The Fish — a hidden confession

Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior.

The early church, under persecution, drew a simple fish to know one another. Its Greek name, ΙΧΘΥΣ (ichthys), spelled a whole creed: Iēsous Christos, Theou Huios, Sōtēr — “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior.”

One quiet line said everything. And it echoes His call to the first disciples — ordinary fishermen — “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.”

“… I will make you fishers of men.” · Matthew 4:19
MannaFish

Put the two together and you have the whole purpose: the Bread of the Word, carried on the sign of the Fish. We take one word of God — your manna for today — and place it in your hands on the fish that confesses Him. Then we teach you to hand one to the next person. It all lives in a single chapter, John 6 — where five loaves and two small fishes fed a multitude, and Jesus called Himself the Bread from heaven.
